title: Vispectra: A compiler for spectroscopic file formats
description:
Vispectra is a cross-platform, browser-based compiler and visualizer for spectroscopic file formats (UV-Vis, XRD, XPS, Raman, IR). It infers the grammatical structure of heterogeneous instrument outputs from a statistical sample of their data, builds a structural contract (the canon), and applies it to the rest. The parser handles American and European number formats, mixed notation within a single row, hard separators (semicolons, spaces, tabs), sparse files, and wide-format blocks. It never guesses silently: when the structure is truly ambiguous, it degrades to user intervention; when it is unambiguous, it commits to a deterministic resolution. The visualization engine renders publication-quality plots with hybrid SVG/Canvas, MinMaxLTTB downsampling for massive datasets, and full visual state serialization to YAML.

The compiler addresses the problem of reading messy, heterogeneous instrument files and relates to the positive-only grammatical inference problem (Gold, 1967). This release (v0.1.1-alpha) ships the complete parser pipeline (phases 00-09), a two-level canonical model, real-world UV-Vis fixtures, and the visualization engine. All processing is client-side in the browser: zero telemetry, no backend dependencies, no data leaves the machine.
